Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Surdas wrote Sursagar (on Krishna's childhood), the Sufi poet Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote Padmavat (1540) in Awadhi, Kabir's verses are compiled in the Bijak, and Jnaneshwar wrote the Jnaneshwari, a Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita. Kabir's verses also appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.question:
[Q.122 · Bihar]
Consider the following statements:
1. Vaishali was the capital of the Vajji (Vrijji) confederacy, of which the Licchavis were the leading clan.
2. Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali.
3. Mahavira attained Kaivalya (supreme knowledge) at Pavapuri.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Vaishali was the seat of the Licchavi-led Vajji gana-sangha, one of the earliest republics, and Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near it. Statement 3 is wrong: Mahavira attained Kaivalya at Jrimbhikagrama on the bank of the Rijupalika river; Pavapuri (Nalanda district) is where he attained nirvana. His mother Trishala was a Licchavi princess.

questions.question:
[Q.123 · Bihar]
Which one of the following is NOT associated with Sher Shah Suri?
options: Rebuilding of the Sarak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road)
questions.explanation: The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar, not Sher Shah. Sher Shah (1540–45), born Farid, issued the silver rupiya of about 178 grains, rebuilt the road from Sonargaon to the Indus (Sarak-e-Azam, later the Grand Trunk Road) and is buried in an octagonal tomb in a lake at Sasaram (Rohtas). His land-revenue measurement system was later adopted by Akbar's minister Todar Mal.

questions.question:
[Q.124 · Bihar]
Bhikhari Thakur, called the 'Shakespeare of Bhojpuri', is associated with which folk theatre form of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bhikhari Thakur (1887–1971) of Saran developed Bidesiya, a folk drama about the pain of migrant labourers and the wives they leave behind. Jat-Jatin and Jhijhiya are folk dances of Mithila, not theatre forms linked to him. Sama-Chakeva, another Mithila festival of the Kartik month, celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters.

questions.question:
[Q.125 · General Mental Ability]
In a certain code language, SALT is written as 2#7@ and TEAM is written as @5#9. How will MALE be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: From SALT = 2#7@: S=2, A=#, L=7, T=@. From TEAM = @5#9: T=@ (consistent), E=5, A=# (consistent), M=9. So MALE = M A L E = 9 # 7 5. Option A swaps the codes for L and E.

questions.question:
[Q.126 · General Mental Ability]
Three of the following four letter groups are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: In BDF, HJL and NPR each letter is two places after the previous one (+2, +2). In TVY the gaps are +2 and +3 (T→V→Y), so it is the odd one; the matching group would have been TVX.

questions.question:
[Q.127 · General Mental Ability]
In a row of 45 students facing north, Ravi is 17th from the left end and Sohan is 21st from the right end. How many students are there between Ravi and Sohan?
questions.explanation: Sohan's position from the left = 45 − 21 + 1 = 25th. Ravi is 17th from the left, so the students between them = 25 − 17 − 1 = 7. A common error is to forget the −1 and answer 8.

questions.question:
[Q.128 · General Mental Ability]
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:40?
questions.explanation: Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30×4 − 5.5×40| = |120 − 220| = 100°. The hour hand moves 0.5° per minute, so at 4:40 it has moved 20° beyond the 4 (to 140°), while the minute hand is at 240°; the difference is 100°.

questions.question:
[Q.129 · General Mental Ability]
A square is divided by drawing both of its diagonals. How many triangles are there in the resulting figure?
questions.explanation: The two diagonals create 4 small triangles meeting at the centre. Each diagonal also divides the square into 2 large triangles, giving 2 × 2 = 4 more. Total = 4 + 4 = 8, which is not among options A–C, so 'None of the above' is correct.

questions.question:
[Q.130 · General Mental Ability]
Kilogram : Mass :: Ampere : ?
questions.explanation: The kilogram is the SI unit of mass; likewise the ampere is the SI unit of electric current. Voltage is measured in volt, resistance in ohm and power in watt. Both kilogram and ampere are among the seven SI base units.

questions.question:
[Q.131 · General Mental Ability]
Statements:
All roses are flowers.
Some flowers are red.
Conclusions:
I. Some roses are red.
II. Some flowers are roses.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
questions.explanation: Since all roses are flowers, at least some flowers are roses, so II follows (conversion of 'All A are B' gives 'Some B are A'). Conclusion I does not follow: the red flowers may lie entirely outside the set of roses. Two particular/general premises like these never give a definite link between roses and red.

questions.question:
[Q.132 · General Mental Ability]
Arrange the following words in the order in which they would appear in a dictionary:
1. Pottery
2. Potassium
3. Postal
4. Potion
questions.explanation: Postal comes first because its third letter 's' precedes 't'. Among the 'pot-' words, the fourth letters are a (Potassium), i (Potion) and t (Pottery). So the order is Postal, Potassium, Potion, Pottery = 3-2-4-1.

questions.question:
[Q.133 · Arithmetic/Maths]
The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹50. What is the sum?

[Q.134 · Arithmetic/Maths]
A train 240 m long crosses a platform 360 m long in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: To cross a platform the train covers its own length plus the platform's: 240 + 360 = 600 m. Speed = 600/30 = 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h. Using only the train's length (240 m) would give a wrong 28.8 km/h.

questions.question:
[Q.135 · Bihar]
What is true of the 7th Khelo India Youth Games held in Bihar in May 2025?
options: The mascot of the Games was 'Gajasimha'
Events were held in Patna, Rajgir, Gaya, Begusarai and Bhagalpur
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: All three are correct, so the answer is 'More than one of the above'. The Games (4–15 May 2025) were Bihar's first time hosting KIYG; Maharashtra topped with 158 medals (58 gold), followed by Haryana and Rajasthan, and the mascot Gajasimha combined an elephant and a lion. Host Bihar won 36 medals (7 gold); a few events such as shooting and cycling were held in New Delhi.

questions.question:
[Q.136 · Bihar]
India won the Men's Hockey Asia Cup 2025, held at Rajgir (Bihar), by defeating which team in the final?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: India beat defending champions South Korea 4–1 in the final on 7 September 2025 at the Rajgir Sports Complex, winning their fourth Asia Cup title and qualifying for the 2026 FIH Men's World Cup. India had beaten China 7–0 in the Super 4s to reach the final. India's earlier Asia Cup titles came in 2003, 2007 and 2017.

questions.question:
[Q.137 · Bihar]
The National Makhana Board, announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, was formally launched by the Prime Minister on 15 September 2025 at
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister launched the National Makhana Board at Purnea on 15 September 2025, at an event where projects worth about ₹40,000 crore were inaugurated or begun. Darbhanga is a tempting distractor because it hosts the ICAR National Research Centre for Makhana. Bihar produces the bulk of India's makhana; Mithila Makhana received a GI tag in 2022.

questions.question:
[Q.138 · Bihar]
Punaura Dham in Sitamarhi, where the foundation stone of a temple complex worth about ₹883 crore was laid in August 2025, is traditionally regarded as
options: The birthplace of the poet Vidyapati
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Punaura Dham is revered as the birthplace (prakatya sthal) of Mata Sita (Janaki). Union Home Minister Amit Shah and CM Nitish Kumar laid the foundation stone on 8 August 2025 after the state cabinet sanctioned ₹882.87 crore. Vidyapati was born at Bisfi (Madhubani), and Mahavira's nirvana took place at Pavapuri.

questions.question:
[Q.139 · Bihar]
Land is being acquired near the ruins of the ancient Vikramshila Mahavihara, at Antichak, for the proposed Central University of Vikramshila. In which district is this?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Vikramshila ruins and the proposed Central University site are at Antichak in the Kahalgaon area of Bhagalpur district. The Centre approved the university in 2015 with ₹500 crore, but it was delayed by land identification; in 2025 the Bihar government sanctioned about ₹88 crore to acquire land at Antichak. Banka is a common distractor because it borders Bhagalpur.

questions.question:
[Q.140 · Current Affairs (National)]
In October 2025 the Union Cabinet approved the Terms of Reference of the 8th Central Pay Commission. Who is its Chairperson?
questions.explanation: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th CPC; Prof. Pulak Ghosh (IIM Bangalore) is part-time member and Pankaj Jain is member-secretary (Cabinet decision of 28 October 2025). The Commission is to report within 18 months, and its recommendations are normally expected to take effect from 1 January 2026. Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th Finance Commission and Justice A. K. Mathur chaired the 7th CPC.

questions.question:
[Q.141 · Current Affairs (National)]
In Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 (results announced in July 2025), which city was ranked the cleanest city in the category of population above 10 lakh, apart from the cities placed in the new 'Super Swachh League'?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad was ranked first among cities with over 10 lakh population, followed by Bhopal and Lucknow. Indore, Surat, Navi Mumbai and Vijayawada were placed in the new Super Swachh League for consistent top performers, with Indore retaining its top status. This 9th edition carried the theme 'Reduce, Reuse, Recycle'; Prayagraj was named the best Ganga town.

[Q.142 · Current Affairs (National)]
Which team topped the medal tally of the 38th National Games held in Uttarakhand in 2025?
questions.explanation: Services (SSCB) topped the table with 68 gold among 121 medals and won the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy. Maharashtra won more medals in all (201) but fewer golds (54), and the table is ranked by gold medals first; Haryana was third. The Games (28 January–14 February 2025) had the Himalayan monal-inspired mascot 'Mauli'.

[Q.143 · Current Affairs (National)]
Madhav Tiger Reserve, notified in March 2025 as India's 58th tiger reserve, is located in which State?
questions.explanation: Madhav National Park in Shivpuri district, Madhya Pradesh, became India's 58th tiger reserve in March 2025 and Madhya Pradesh's ninth. Madhya Pradesh, the 'Tiger State', also had the 57th, Ratapani (December 2024). Tiger reserves are notified by state governments on the advice of the National Tiger Conservation Authority.

[Q.144 · Miscellaneous]
Match List-I (Book) with List-II (Author):
List-I
a. India Wins Freedom
b. Hind Swaraj
c. Unhappy India
d. The Discovery of India
List-II
1. Lala Lajpat Rai
2. Jawaharlal Nehru
3. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
4. M. K. Gandhi
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: India Wins Freedom is Maulana Azad's autobiographical account; Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in Gujarati in 1909 aboard ship from London to South Africa; Lala Lajpat Rai wrote Unhappy India (1928) as a reply to Katherine Mayo's 'Mother India'; Nehru wrote The Discovery of India in Ahmednagar Fort jail (1942–46).

[Q.145 · Current Affairs (International)]
The United Nations marked its 80th anniversary on 24 October 2025. Who served as President of the 80th session of the UN General Assembly (September 2025–September 2026)?
questions.explanation: Former German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock was elected on 2 June 2025 (167 votes in a vote Russia requested) as President of the 80th UNGA session; she is the first woman from the Western European and Others Group to hold the post. Philemon Yang (Cameroon) presided over the 79th session and Dennis Francis (Trinidad and Tobago) the 78th. Helga Schmid was Germany's earlier nominee.

[Q.146 · Current Affairs (International)]
Who was sworn in as the Prime Minister of Bangladesh in February 2026 after the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)-led alliance won the parliamentary election?
questions.explanation: BNP chairman Tarique Rahman, son of Ziaur Rahman and Khaleda Zia, took oath on 17 February 2026 after the BNP and its partners won 212 of 350 seats; a Jamaat-e-Islami-led alliance (77 seats) became the opposition. Muhammad Yunus had led the interim government that conducted the election after Sheikh Hasina's ouster in August 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.147 · Current Affairs (International)]
What is true of the advisory opinion on the obligations of States in respect of climate change delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in July 2025?
options: It was given at the request of the UN General Assembly
The resolution seeking the opinion was spearheaded by Vanuatu
It is legally binding on all UN member states
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A and B are correct, so the answer is 'More than one of the above'. The UNGA requested the opinion in March 2023 on a Vanuatu-led initiative begun by Pacific students, and on 23 July 2025 the ICJ unanimously held that States have obligations under international law to protect the climate system. C is wrong: advisory opinions carry great legal authority but are not binding.

[Q.148 · Current Affairs (International)]
Which of the following won the Booker Prize 2025?
options: Kiran Desai – The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny
questions.explanation: David Szalay won the Booker Prize on 10 November 2025 for 'Flesh', becoming the first Hungarian-British winner; the judging panel was chaired by Roddy Doyle. Kiran Desai's novel was on the 2025 shortlist, Samantha Harvey's 'Orbital' won in 2024, and Banu Mushtaq's 'Heart Lamp' (translated by Deepa Bhasthi) won the International Booker Prize 2025.

questions.question:
[Q.149 · Current Affairs (International)]
Which country topped the medal table at the 2026 Winter Olympics held in Milano Cortina, Italy?
questions.explanation: Norway topped the table with 18 gold and 41 medals in all, ahead of the United States (12 gold, a US Winter Games record). Host Italy had its best-ever Winter Games but placed fourth. The Games were held from 6 to 22 February 2026; the 2030 Winter Olympics go to the French Alps.

questions.question:
[Q.150 · Current Affairs (International)]
Consider the following statements regarding the WHO Pandemic Agreement (status as of 1 October 2026):
1. It was adopted by the 78th World Health Assembly in May 2025.
2. It will be opened for signature only after the World Health Assembly adopts its annex on the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system.
3. The PABS annex was finalised and adopted by the 79th World Health Assembly in May 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025, and under Article 31 it opens for signature only after the PABS annex is adopted. Statement 3 is wrong: in May 2026 the 79th WHA extended the negotiations, sending the annex to the 80th WHA (May 2027) or a special session, and talks continued in July 2026. The Agreement grew out of lessons from COVID-19.
